description: An examination of fish farming and capture fisheries in Tanzania, covering pond construction and management, fish breeding, harvesting, preservation, marketing and the contribution of fisheries to the national economy.

mcq.questionText: What is the meaning of aquaculture?

options.text: The catching of wild fish from natural water bodies
The deliberate rearing of fish and other aquatic organisms under controlled conditions
The processing and canning of marine fish for export
The study of ocean currents and marine ecosystems

mcq.explanation: Aquaculture (fish farming) is the deliberate keeping and rearing of fish and other aquatic organisms under controlled conditions, unlike capture fisheries which harvest wild stocks.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the most important nutritional reason for promoting fish farming in Tanzania?

options.text: Fish provides a cheap source of high quality animal protein
Fish reduce the number of mosquitoes only
Fish farming requires no labour at all

mcq.explanation: Fish is a rich and relatively cheap source of high quality animal protein, helping to fight protein malnutrition such as kwashiorkor.

mcq.questionText: Which species is the most commonly farmed fish in Tanzanian fresh water ponds?
mcq.explanation: Tilapia (sato), especially Oreochromis species, is the most widely farmed fish in Tanzania because it is hardy, fast growing and easy to feed.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes capture fisheries?

options.text: Rearing fish in artificial ponds and feeding them daily
Harvesting wild fish from lakes, rivers and the ocean
Breeding fish in tanks for sale of fingerlings

mcq.explanation: Capture fisheries involve catching fish from natural water bodies such as Lake Victoria, Lake Tanganyika and the Indian Ocean, rather than rearing them.

mcq.questionText: When siting a fish pond, why should the area have a gentle slope or gradient?

options.text: To make harvesting impossible without machines
To allow the pond to be filled and completely drained by gravity
To increase evaporation of water from the pond
To prevent any water from entering the pond

mcq.explanation: A gentle gradient allows water to flow into the pond and to be drained completely by gravity during harvesting and cleaning, without expensive pumping.

mcq.questionText: Which type of soil is most suitable for constructing the base of a fish pond?

options.text: Sandy soil that drains very quickly
Clay or loamy soil that holds water

mcq.explanation: Clay or clay loam soil is ideal because it holds water and prevents excessive seepage, keeping the pond full.

mcq.questionText: Why is lime (liming) applied to a fish pond before stocking?

options.text: To make the water acidic for fish growth
To correct acidity, disinfect the pond and kill parasites and predators
To colour the water white for visibility
To provide direct food for the fish

mcq.explanation: Liming neutralises acidity, raises pH, disinfects the pond and helps kill disease organisms, parasites and unwanted predators before stocking.

mcq.questionText: Fertilising a fish pond with manure or inorganic fertiliser mainly aims to:

options.text: Promote the growth of natural fish food such as plankton
Reduce the depth of the pond
Increase the acidity of the water
Kill all the weeds in the pond

mcq.explanation: Fertilisers add nutrients that promote the growth of plankton (natural food), which the fish feed on, increasing productivity.

mcq.questionText: The young fish used to stock a newly prepared pond are called:
mcq.explanation: Fingerlings are young fish about the size of a finger used for stocking ponds; they are strong enough to survive and grow.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a method of controlling predators in a fish pond?

options.text: Leaving the pond open to birds
Fencing the pond and screening inlets and outlets
Adding more predators to balance the pond
Stopping the supply of water completely

mcq.explanation: Fencing the pond and fitting screens or nets on the inlet and outlet keeps out predators such as birds, snakes and predatory fish.

mcq.questionText: Why is excessive growth of weeds in a fish pond undesirable?

options.text: Weeds increase dissolved oxygen at all times
Weeds compete for oxygen and nutrients, harbour predators and hinder harvesting
Weeds make the fish grow faster
Weeds have no effect on the pond

mcq.explanation: Dense weeds compete for nutrients and oxygen, give shelter to predators and pests, and make netting and harvesting of fish difficult.

options.text: Keeping fish together with crops or livestock so that they support each other
Rearing only one species of fish in many ponds
Catching fish from the ocean using big trawlers

mcq.explanation: Integrated fish farming combines fish ponds with poultry, pigs or crops; for example poultry droppings fertilise the pond, raising productivity and reducing costs.

mcq.questionText: Which method of fish preservation involves exposing fish to smoke from burning wood?
mcq.explanation: Smoking preserves fish by drying it and depositing smoke chemicals that prevent spoilage, a common low cost method around Lake Victoria and Lake Tanganyika.

mcq.questionText: Which Tanzanian lake is famous for the Nile perch (sangara) export industry?
mcq.explanation: Lake Victoria is the leading source of Nile perch (sangara), which is filleted and exported, earning significant foreign currency for Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a common problem facing fish farming in Tanzania?

options.text: Abundant capital and trained extension staff everywhere
Shortage of capital, quality fingerlings and technical knowledge
Too much rainfall in all regions throughout the year
Excess market demand met fully at all times

mcq.explanation: Fish farmers often face shortage of capital, lack of quality fingerlings and feeds, inadequate technical knowledge and poor markets, which limit production.

fib.questionText: The deliberate rearing of fish under controlled conditions is called _____.
fib.explanation: Aquaculture, or fish farming, is the controlled rearing of fish and other aquatic organisms.

fib.questionText: The most widely farmed fish species in Tanzania, locally known as sato, is _____.
fib.explanation: Tilapia (sato) is hardy, fast growing and easy to manage, making it the most common pond fish in Tanzania.

fib.questionText: Young fish about the size of a finger used to stock a pond are called _____.
fib.explanation: Fingerlings are the young fish strong enough to survive when introduced into a prepared pond.

fib.questionText: Applying lime to a pond to reduce acidity and kill disease organisms is called _____.
fib.explanation: Liming corrects acidity, raises pH and disinfects the pond before stocking.

fib.questionText: The type of soil best suited for holding water in a fish pond is _____ soil.
fib.explanation: Clay or clay loam soil holds water and reduces seepage, keeping the pond full.

fib.questionText: Adding manure or fertiliser to a pond to encourage growth of natural fish food (plankton) is called _____.
fib.explanation: Fertilising increases plankton, the natural food of fish, raising pond productivity.

fib.questionText: Catching wild fish from natural water bodies such as lakes and the ocean is known as _____ fisheries.
fib.explanation: Capture fisheries harvest wild stocks, unlike aquaculture which rears fish.

fib.questionText: Combining fish ponds with crops or livestock such as poultry is called _____ fish farming.
fib.explanation: Integrated fish farming links the pond with other enterprises so wastes from one benefit the other.

fib.questionText: The Tanzanian lake that is the leading source of exported Nile perch (sangara) is Lake _____.
fib.explanation: Lake Victoria supplies most of Tanzania's exported Nile perch fillets.

fib.questionText: Preserving fish by exposing it to smoke from burning wood is called _____.
fib.explanation: Smoking dries the fish and deposits smoke chemicals that prevent spoilage.

tf.questionText: Aquaculture is the catching of wild fish from natural lakes and the ocean.
tf.explanation: Aquaculture is the deliberate rearing of fish under controlled conditions; catching wild fish is capture fisheries.

tf.questionText: Fish is an important and relatively cheap source of high quality animal protein.
tf.explanation: Fish supplies high quality protein at a relatively low cost, helping to combat protein malnutrition.

tf.questionText: Sandy soil that drains quickly is the best soil for the base of a fish pond.
tf.explanation: Clay or loamy soil that holds water is best; sandy soil loses water through seepage.

tf.questionText: A gentle gradient at the pond site allows water to fill and drain the pond by gravity.
tf.explanation: A gentle slope lets water enter and be drained by gravity, easing filling, cleaning and harvesting.

tf.questionText: Liming a pond increases acidity and encourages disease organisms.
tf.explanation: Liming reduces acidity, raises pH and disinfects the pond, killing many disease organisms.

tf.questionText: Fertilising a fish pond helps to increase plankton, which is natural food for the fish.
tf.explanation: Fertilisers add nutrients that boost plankton growth, providing more natural food for fish.

tf.questionText: Overstocking a pond with too many fish leads to stunted growth due to competition for food and oxygen.
tf.explanation: Too many fish compete for limited food and oxygen, so growth is poor; correct stocking density is important.

tf.questionText: Tilapia (sato) is one of the main fish species farmed in Tanzanian ponds.
tf.explanation: Tilapia, together with catfish (kambale), is among the leading species farmed in Tanzania.

tf.questionText: Integrated fish farming combines fish ponds with crops or livestock to use resources efficiently.
tf.explanation: In integrated systems, wastes such as poultry droppings fertilise the pond while pond mud and water can serve crops.

tf.questionText: Lake Tanganyika and Lake Nyasa make no contribution to Tanzania's fisheries.
tf.explanation: Lakes Tanganyika and Nyasa are major capture fisheries supplying fish such as dagaa and many endemic species, contributing food, income and employment.

summary.correctAnswer: Aquaculture is the deliberate rearing of fish and other aquatic organisms under controlled conditions for food and income.
summary.explanation: It distinguishes farmed fish from wild fish obtained through capture fisheries.

summary.questionText: State three reasons why fish farming is important in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: It provides cheap high quality protein, generates income from sales, and creates employment.
summary.explanation: Fish farming improves nutrition, raises farmers' incomes and provides jobs in production, processing and marketing.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between capture fisheries and aquaculture.
summary.correctAnswer: Capture fisheries involve catching wild fish from natural waters, while aquaculture is rearing fish under controlled conditions.
summary.explanation: The key difference is wild harvesting versus deliberate controlled rearing.

summary.questionText: Mention two factors to consider when siting a fish pond.
summary.correctAnswer: A reliable water supply and suitable water holding soil such as clay, on land with a gentle gradient.
summary.explanation: Adequate clean water, water retentive soil and a gentle slope are essential for a successful pond.

summary.questionText: Outline the main steps in preparing a pond before stocking with fish.
summary.correctAnswer: Drain and clean the pond, apply lime, then fertilise with manure to grow plankton before adding fingerlings.
summary.explanation: Liming and fertilising prepare a healthy, productive environment for the fingerlings.

summary.questionText: Why is liming carried out in fish pond management?
summary.correctAnswer: Liming reduces acidity, raises pH, disinfects the pond and kills parasites and disease organisms.
summary.explanation: It creates favourable, healthy water conditions for fish.

summary.questionText: List two methods used to control predators in a fish pond.
summary.correctAnswer: Fencing the pond and fitting screens or nets on the inlet and outlet to keep out birds, snakes and predatory fish.
summary.explanation: Physical barriers prevent predators from entering and eating the stock.

summary.questionText: Mention two methods of harvesting fish from a pond.
summary.correctAnswer: Using nets such as seine nets, or draining the pond and collecting the fish.
summary.explanation: Netting allows partial harvesting while draining gives a complete harvest.

summary.questionText: State three methods of preserving fish.
summary.correctAnswer: Smoking, salting (and drying), and freezing or refrigeration.
summary.explanation: These methods prevent spoilage so fish can be stored, transported and marketed.

summary.questionText: Explain the contribution of fisheries to the Tanzanian economy.
summary.correctAnswer: Fisheries from Lakes Victoria, Tanganyika, Nyasa and the Indian Ocean provide food, income, employment, raw materials and foreign exchange through exports such as Nile perch.
summary.explanation: The sector supports livelihoods, nutrition and national revenue.

hoq.questionText: A farmer near Mwanza wants to start a tilapia pond on sloping land with sandy soil and a small stream nearby. Which advice is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Build the pond on the sandy soil as it is, because sand holds water well
Line or puddle the pond base with clay to reduce seepage, use the gentle slope for gravity filling and draining, and screen the stream inlet
Abandon the project because no site in Tanzania is suitable for tilapia
Fill the pond with sea water to make the tilapia grow faster

hoq.explanation: Sandy soil leaks water, so the base should be sealed with clay; the gentle slope aids gravity filling and draining, and screening the inlet keeps out predators. Tilapia are freshwater fish, so sea water is wrong.

hoq.questionText: A fish farmer notices that, although feeding is regular, the fish are small and many die, and the water often smells and looks green and thick. What is the MOST likely cause and best remedy?

options.text: The pond is overstocked and over fertilised causing low oxygen; reduce stocking density and control fertiliser and weed growth
There are too few fish; add many more fingerlings immediately
The fish need salt water; add table salt until the pond is salty
The pond has too much oxygen; stop all water inflow permanently

hoq.explanation: Stunted growth, deaths and thick green water indicate overstocking and excessive plankton (over fertilising) leading to oxygen shortage. The remedy is to reduce stocking density and manage fertiliser and weeds to restore good water quality.

hoq.questionText: A smallholder keeps both poultry and a fish pond and wants to lower feed costs while raising pond output. Which practice BEST achieves this through integrated fish farming?

options.text: Position the poultry house so droppings fertilise the pond, boosting plankton that feeds the fish
Sell all the poultry and rely only on bought commercial fish feed
Keep the pond and poultry completely separate and far apart so they never interact
Pour disinfectant into the pond daily to kill all organisms including plankton

hoq.explanation: In integrated fish farming, poultry droppings act as organic fertiliser that promotes plankton growth, providing natural fish food and reducing the need for bought feed, raising productivity at low cost.
